messages:
andrea: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC — we need to finalize the rollout controls for per-model flags and fallback behavior. Posting a short checklist and questions.

mike: +1. Do we still want the dual-flag approach (enable_kernel_x + allow_fallback)?

jain: I think so. Dual flags give ops explicit opt-in for new kernels and a separate safety net toggle to allow graceful fallback. Keeps deployment surface small.

sasha: One nuance: some models depend on kv-cache layout invariants. If fast-attn-v2 changes cache positioning, a silent fallback could corrupt streaming state. We should gate fallback for streams.

andrea: Good catch. Proposal: fallback allowed by default for stateless generation, but for streaming/chat routes we require explicit per-model opt-in to allow fallback. That way we fail closed for streaming unless owner flips allow_fallback.

mike: Sounds reasonable. How do we represent that in model config? Example we discussed:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-open-7b",
  "kernel_flags": {
    "enable": ["fast-attn-v2"],
    "allow_fallback": false,
    "fallback_policy": "compat-attn"
  },
  "routes": {
    "chat_stream": {"allow_fallback": false},
    "batch": {"allow_fallback": true}
  }
}
```

jain: That's clear. Implementation note: runtime should check route-level override -> model-level flag -> global default. Also we need an admin API to flip flags without a model release.

andrea: Agreed. Admin API + console UI. Ops needs an audit trail. rollout-bot: (automated) Recorded change: feature flag schema v2 accepted for staging.

sasha: Monitoring plan: we need spike detectors on token-level perplexity deltas, error rates (invalid-kv, stream-reset), and latency regressions when a kernel is enabled. If any alert fires, auto-roll back the kernel for that cohort.

mike: For canarying, propose traffic buckets: 1% initial canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. For per-model we use model-owner tagging to start at 5% by default. Admin can force 100% for dedicated customers.

jain: Also add a safety TTL for kernel experiments. If a canary is active >48h without explicit sign-off, auto-disable. Prevents accidental long-lived experiments.

andrea: Action items: 1) @mike implement admin API + audit (ETA EOD Wed). 2) @sasha add stream-safe check and disallow fallback-by-default for streaming routes (ETA Thu). 3) @jain add metrics + alert rules to ops-signal (ETA Fri). 4) @mike wire canary percentages into rollout-bot for automated promotion (ETA next Tue).

mike: I'll open a small PR for the admin endpoint and a migration for feature schema v2. Will tag for review.

jain: For the alerts, I'll start with these metrics:
- token_error_rate (invalid-kv, decode-errors)
- mean_stream_reset_per_min
- generation_latency_p50/p95
- output_quality_delta (eval set scoring)
I'll post a sample Grafana dashboard in the tickets.

andrea: Good. One more thing — fallback semantics: we must ensure fallbacks preserve request-level deterministic IDs so tracing + billing remain correct. runtime should attach a fallback_reason tag when it falls back. ops-signal: can you ensure the tracing pipeline picks that up?

ops-signal: Yep — will add fallback_reason to the trace span and expose a fallback count metric by reason.

sasha: If we run into cache-incompatibility cases, we should consider an explicit cache-warm migration path instead of blind fallback. Marking as future work in the RFC follow-up doc.

andrea: OK team — lets track these in the post-RFC project board. I'll file the card and link PRs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

rollout-bot: (automated) Created post-rfc project: "kernel-rollout-controls" and added cards for admin-api, stream-safety, metrics, and rollout-automation.
